lede: Tuesday is the week's heaviest day for anyone paying attention to how this town is governed: a newly seated Town Council takes up second reading of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code — a real vote on land-use amendments affecting landscaping and historic review — while the Telluride Housing Authority meets to hash out primary residency policy for dependents in split-custody households, a quiet but consequential question for working families here. Thursday, Planning and Zoning digs into three Town-owned development projects in the Accommodations 2 zone, including the Carhenge Redevelopment, which involves a large-scale subdivision and concept plan review at 700 W Pacific.

notable.stake: Second reading vote on wildfire code changes to land use, landscaping, and historic review.
New residency policy for split-custody dependents could affect housing eligibility for local families.
P&Z reviews subdivision and concept plans for three Town-owned development sites, including Carhenge.
